label: 40' / 12 m — 4V Configuration Two
planNote: The 40' / 12 m sheet documents TWO configurations from one panel set. This file is Configuration Two — a 5/8 sphere on a short (roughly 1') pony wall, tall enough for two storeys. Both configurations use the Deep Frame Method: the struts are FULL 2x6 on edge (1 1/2" x 5 1/2" / 38 x 140 mm), not the ripped 1 5/16" x 1 1/2" stock the smaller 4V plans use, so every end cut is a compound miter-and-bevel. The four panel shapes are identical to Configuration One — only the counts, the pony wall and the doorway change. Build from these printed dimensions; the app's generated 3D model uses a standard Class I 4V breakdown and its computed dimensions differ.

overview.summary: Configuration Two of the 40-foot (12 m) 4V dome: a 5/8 sphere carried on a short pony wall — 38'-5 3/16" (11714 mm) wide and 26'-5 1/4" (8059 mm) tall overall, with the wall itself only 11 7/8" (302 mm) high on the front elevation and the doorway roof reaching 11'-6 9/16" (3519 mm) on the side elevation. The shell is 192 regular panels in the same four shapes as Configuration One (114 Hexagon, 30 Pentagon, 34 Triangle 1, 14 Triangle 2) and NO special dome panels: the doorway here is a framed gabled porch that stands clear of the shell instead of cutting into it. Every member is a full 2x6 stood on edge — the Deep Frame Method — so each strut end carries both a miter (the flat setting) and a bevel (the tilt setting), and the plan gives both for every end. The pony wall ring measures 38'-0 1/2" (11595 mm) across and 35'-10 1/4" (10928 mm) the other way; with the doorway walls projecting the footprint is 41'-1 15/16" (12545 mm) deep, and the doorway opening between the two wing walls is 17'-4 11/16" (5301 mm). The sheet also gives two alternative floor systems (radial and conventional), a doorway deck, and an optional five-sided cupola at the crown. Printed areas: dome surface 1150 sq ft (107 sq m), wall surface 140 sq ft (13 sq m), floor surface 1150 sq ft (107 sq m).

notes: This dome is meant to be built with the Deep Frame Method using 2x6 framing timbers at a minimum (1.5 x 5.5" / 38 mm x 140 mm actual). Fasteners rated for structural use are required.

This is a very large and tall structure. It will require very tall scaffolding, timbers to help hold up the structure as it gets built, and potentially heavy equipment. Configuration Two is the taller of the two — 26'-5 1/4" (8059 mm) to the crown.

All panel miter angles on these plans are stated as degrees OFF 90 — that is the number you dial into the saw, not the interior angle of the triangle. In the Deep Frame Method each end also carries a bevel: the vertical angle on the jig becomes the miter (flat) setting on the saw, and the horizontal angle on the jig becomes the bevel (vertical) setting.

Configuration Two uses NO special dome panels. Where Configuration One cuts a mirrored pair of Partial Triangle 1 panels and a Door Header Panel into the shell to make room for its doorway, Configuration Two frames a gabled porch that stands clear of the shell, so all 192 panels are full regular panels.

DEEP FRAME METHOD — MAKING A JIG (pp.55-59). Exact strut measurements are given for convenience, but you can also find them yourself, and check your accuracy, by building a jig for each panel. Cut the struts as prescribed, assemble a panel and check its overall length; within 1/16" on each side is good, and a smidge small is better than a smidge big. To make a jig, find a solid flat piece of material just bigger than the panel. Mark a straight line and two points on it the distance apart of the panel's bottom edge. Using a straight piece of wood, hammer two nails through it the panel's side length apart; using the two bottom marks as pivots, scratch an arc with the second nail. Where the two arcs meet is the third mark. Connect the dots, and if you want, carefully cut the material away. Then make template rails: cut blocks with the bevel angle on the end (5.1 degrees in this case) and attach them to a flat surface so you have something to clamp your material to, arranged so they do not interfere with the struts or each other. Clamp the framing material to the rails, take the angles with a digital angle finder, cut the initial miters, repeat for the final miters, and cut the excess off flush with the intersecting panel. You can set stop blocks and cut all your struts ahead of time, then assemble with structural rated screws or nails.

PANEL ORIENTATION (p60). When you assemble the panels in groups, make sure they are oriented correctly: the 'Bottom' measurements given in the plans are always arrayed to the OUTSIDE of the group. This reciprocal framing creates an extremely stable structure.

FLOOR — RADIAL FRAME (pp.17-19). The radial deck design can be much easier to produce and lay out for a beginner builder. It is a good idea to run blocking underneath subfloor seams and use tongue and groove material. Girders: (5) girders @ 22'-5 11/16" (6850 mm) long to long 18 degrees — can be split in the middle; (3) girders @ 12'-1 7/16" (3694 mm) long to long 30 degrees; (16) post / pier assembly. The imperial sheet calls both sizes '4x10 girders'. Girder layout dimensions: outer pentagon sides 11'-2 7/8" (3425 mm) and 22'-5 11/16" (6851 mm), across 34'-9 15/16" (10615 mm) and 22'-7 9/16" (6898 mm), point to point 36'-7 7/16" (11161 mm), centre height 19'-3" (5868 mm), 15'-6 15/16" (4748 mm), 11'-11 3/8" (3641 mm); inner triangle 12'-1 7/16" (3695 mm) and 12'-7 13/16" (3856 mm) with a 7'-3 5/8" (2226 mm) offset.

FLOOR — RADIAL FRAME JOISTS (p19). All framing members 2x10 (38 x 235 mm). (20) joists @ 16' (4877 mm); (20) rim @ 6'-0 1/4" (1835 mm) long to long, 9 deg; (20) outer block @ 4'-9" (1448 mm) long to long, 9 deg; (20) inner block @ 2'-6 13/16" (783 mm) long to long, 9 deg; (20) inner rim @ 11 11/16" (297 mm) long to long, 9 deg; (40) mid span joists @ 3'-6 1/8" (1070 mm); (20) mid span joists @ 6'-9 1/16" (2059 mm); (2) centre joists @ 4'-5 13/16" (1367 mm) long to long, 36 deg; (1) centre joist @ 5'-10 7/8" (1800 mm). Overall diameter 38'-0 5/16" (11590 mm).

FLOOR — CONVENTIONAL FRAME (pp.20-22). The conventional deck design allows for efficient use of standard size materials, built at standard, consistent spans. 28 post / piers. All framing members 2x10 (38 x 235 mm). Regular joists: (27) @ 11'-9" (3581 mm); (10) @ 12'-9 3/16" (3891 mm). Special joists: (4) 12'-5 1/2" (3797 mm) LP 18 deg; (4) 12'-0 5/16" (3666 mm) LP 18 deg; (4) 11'-7 1/16" (3523 mm printed metric) LP 18 deg; (4) 11'-1 7/8" (3400 mm) LP 18 deg; (4) 10'-5 7/8" (3197 mm) LP 36 deg; (4) 9'-6 1/4" (2902 mm) LP 36 deg; (4) 8'-6 5/8" (2607 mm) LP 36 deg; (4) 7'-7" (2311 mm) LP 36 deg; (4) 5'-10 15/16" (1802 mm) LP 54 deg; (4) 4'-0 15/16" (1243 mm) LP 54 deg; (4) 1'-10 3/16" (564 mm) LP 72 deg; (2) 7'-8 15/16" (2361 mm) long to long 72 deg. Girder: (2) 13'-10 15/16" (4240 mm) LP 18 deg; (2) 5'-11 7/16" (1815 mm) LP 18 deg; (2) 5'-10 15/16" (1802 mm) LP 18 deg; (2) 13'-11 7/16" (4253 mm) LP 18 deg; (4) 16' (4877 mm). Frame dimensions: 38'-0 5/16" (11590 mm) across, 35'-10 7/8" (10945 mm) long to long 18 deg, bay widths 11'-9" (3581 mm) and 12'-9 3/16" (3891 mm), perimeter facet 6'-0 1/4" (1836 mm) long to long 18 deg.

FLOOR — CONVENTIONAL FRAME FOOTER LAYOUT (p21). 28 post / piers on a square grid 38'-0 5/16" (11590 mm) on a side, diagonal 26'-10 11/16" (8196 mm). Grid offsets from the centre line, both directions: 3'-0 3/16" (919 mm), 4'-0" (1219 mm) [6'-0" (1829 mm) on the vertical], 8'-8 7/8" (2664 mm), 12'-0" (3658 mm), 13'-7 3/8" (4149 mm), 17'-1 13/16" (5228 mm), 19'-0 3/16" (5795 mm).

CUPOLA (pp.49-54) — optional, five sided, sits over the crown pentagon. Wall, cuts per wall (2x6): studs (2) 1'-3 1/8" (385 mm) long to short 8 deg; plates (2) 4'-9 3/8" (1458 mm) long to long 36 deg; (3) connecting blocks. Connecting blocks: 1'-4 5/8" (422 mm) tall x 4 3/16" (106 mm) wide, laid out on a 3 5/16" (85 mm) square with a 6 15/16" (176 mm) diagonal and 4 3/8" (111 mm) / 2 9/16" (64 mm) offsets; the angled block is 1'-3 1/8" (385 mm) at 8 deg. Window frame: 4'-9 3/8" (1458 mm) wide with 36 deg ends, 1'-6" (457 mm) tall overall, 1'-3" (381 mm) glazed opening. Partial pentagon (to create the cupola opening): cut and replace the centre strut in a regular panel with 4'-3 5/8" (1312 mm) long to long 35.7 deg; the resulting opening is 4'-1 3/8" (1254 mm) across the top, 5'-6 5/8" (1692 mm) across the bottom, 1'-0" (305 mm) high, 1'-2 3/4" (375 mm) on the slope. Full pentagon (you can just as well use full pentagon frames): place a centre strut in the regular panel at 3'-11 15/16" (1217 mm) long to long 35.7 deg, 1'-0" (305 mm) up from the base, with 2'-10 5/8" (880 mm) above it. Fascia: (5) 5'-7 11/16" (1719 mm) long to long, 8 deg miter, 20 deg bevel. The cupola also carries elongated cover material, operable windows and a fascia over the top pentagon frames.
